manifest.name: dsh-unified-model
manifest.description: Switch model and reasoning effort across every DeepSeek Harness session at once — one control, all conversations, effort included.

bundle.text:
# Bundle layer for the unified model/effort control: one Host row that owns the
# batch routes, and its browser half declared through `dsh.client`.
- insert:
    - id: unified-model
      name: 'dsh-unified-model'

readme.text:
**Switch model and reasoning effort across every DeepSeek Harness session at once — one control, all conversations, effort included.**

[中文](README.zh.md)

DeepSeek Harness stores the model choice **per session**. The shipped default-model setting only covers sessions that have not chosen one yet, and `/model` only ever changes the session you are in. So there is no built-in way to move a whole session history onto one model/effort pair at once.

This plugin adds that missing control to the composer row:

```
[⇉ All sessions]  [ deepseek-v4.1-flash ▾ ]
                   ^ the shipped model picker, untouched
```

In a narrow window the button collapses to its glyph so it stops competing for room with the model picker:

```
[⇉]  [ deepseek-v4.1-flash ▾ ]
```

The same control stays reachable either way — the full name lives in the button's `title` and `aria-label`, so the icon-only form is not an unlabelled mystery.

Open it, pick a provider, a model and a thinking effort, and choose the scope:

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **Every session** | writes the selection into every session that can hold its own |
| **Every other session** | same, but leaves the session you are looking at untouched |
| **Also make this the default** | additionally writes the deployment default, so sessions created later start on it |
A live `done/total` counter runs while the batch is in flight, and the result reports what changed, what already matched, and what failed.

Most "apply a model to all sessions" attempts stop at the model, because effort looks like it belongs to a different layer. It does not:

- `sessionController.selectModel()` takes `{ provider, model, reasoningEffort? }`.
- The selection it commits is appended to the session log as a `model/selection` event, and that event's schema **carries `reasoningEffort`**.
- The `modelSelection` projection re-reads it, and `selectionFor()` restores it after a restart, so the effort survives.

Verified on a live profile: a written session log contains

```json
{"type":"model/selection","seq":4,"data":{"provider":"tencent-intranet","model":"deepseek-v4.1-flash-ioa","reasoningEffort":"max"}}
```

That is why this plugin compares `provider` **and** `model` **and** `reasoningEffort` when it decides whether a session already matches. A plugin that compares only the first two will report success while silently leaving effort unapplied.

| Case | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary sessions | **Updated** — the target of the control |
| Subagent sessions | **Not touched.** They follow their parent's routing and the host rejects per-session selection for them. Counted separately in the result so they are never mistaken for failures |
| A session already carrying the target selection | **Skipped**, no write. A repeat click on an already-unified history finishes in milliseconds |
| A session whose log is corrupt or locked by another process | Reported as **failed** with the host's own reason, and the rest of the batch continues |
The batch runs **on the Host**, not in the browser, so closing the tab does not interrupt it. The client half only starts the run and polls its progress.
It does not patch a shipped plugin, rewrite session logs, or edit projection caches. It calls the same public host API the built-in `/model` dialog calls:

```
sessionController.list({})                  → every session, with its current selection
sessionController.selectModel({ sessionId, provider, model, reasoningEffort })
sessionController.modelCatalog()            → provider groups and each model's published efforts
agentDefaultModel.saveSelection({ … })      → the deployment default, when requested

Because the write path is the official one, session state stays in the official format, uninstalling changes nothing, and a future Harness that renames these methods costs you this plugin only — never the rest of the app.

Three route exist, all behind the composition's connection trust fence:

```
GET  /unified-model/state    → catalog, default, every session's selection, current run
POST /unified-model/apply    → { provider, model, reasoningEffort?, scope, excludeSessionId? } → { runId }
GET  /unified-model/status   → the live run, or the last one
POST /unified-model/default  → write the deployment default

`selectModel` resumes each cold session, which is by far the most expensive part of the operation. So the plugin reads every session's selection from `list()` first and skips matching ones. Measured on a 55-session profile: the first run wrote 36 sessions in **2.7 s**; the immediate repeat skipped 53 and finished in **56 ms**.

An unknown model or an effort the model does not publish makes the adapter reject the request. Both are checked against `modelCatalog()` **before** the first session is touched, so a typo fails the request instead of failing 60 sessions one by one:

```
400 model-unknown       the catalog does not list p/m
400 effort-unsupported  p/m publishes low, medium, high, xhigh, max; ultra999 is not one of them
```

The client offers exactly the levels the model publishes, so the two never disagree.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add dsh-unified-model
```

Or from a checkout:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add link:/path/to/dsh-unified-model
```

Restart the app afterwards — bundle patch layers and client bundles both load at startup.
None. The control appears in the composer row; there is nothing to set up.

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0` or newer.
- The web UI (the control lives in a composer slot).

```sh
npm test      # node --test; covers the selection reader and the skip rules
npm run check # node --check on both halves
```

`index.js` is the Host half (routes, the batch). `client.js` is the browser half (the chip and the panel). `test/selection.test.mjs` pins the one decision that matters: whether a session counts as already correct.
